description: Static trace from captured previous/next response controls through the imported client selection helper and its optimistic/persist/rollback sequence.

reviewed_stages.detail: The response-version control reads an ordered list of variant message identities and the active variant index from scoped client state.
Previous and next buttons are rendered only when multiple variants exist and an active index is available; each is disabled at its respective boundary or while selection is busy.
The click handler resolves the requested variant index to an identity and calls an imported conversation-selection helper. An error notification is shown if that call rejects.

The selection helper checks that a conversation and requested mapped variant exist, that an incompatible active state is absent, and that a candidate selected descendant can be derived and validated against the graph.

Before making the persistence request, the helper marks selection busy, changes the locally selected node, updates dependent scoped conversation state, and invalidates relevant cached conversation data.
The helper constructs a request to update the selected current node for the conversation and treats an unsuccessful response as a selection failure. No actual server response was captured.

On failure, the helper restores the previous selected node if its optimistic selection is still current. In a finalization path it reconciles the mapping/current-node state and clears the selection-busy flag.

confirmation_scope: The source establishes a selection request and local optimistic/failure behavior. It does not establish a real persisted backend change or the current deployed contract.
caveats: Some other client paths use direct local selected-node updates rather than this persisted response-version control.
The mapping lookup may choose a descendant of a response variant; variant identity and final selected current node need not always coincide.
An optimistic client update can temporarily affect rendering before a server confirms the request.
Displayed response-version controls are subject to client gates and might not appear for all accounts or conversations.
This source-level trace does not establish actual button clicks, server acknowledgement, durable persistence or a complete deployed API protocol.
privacy: Only authored summaries, technical operation labels and capture-local resource ordinals are published; no original request path, full source snippet, user message, account token or identity is included.
